title: Jewellery sold as sterling silver on Amazon and Temu found to contain toxic chemicals
description: Image source, HandoutsImage caption, Meranda suffered skin irritation after buying a necklace sold as sterling silverByGeorge SandemanJewellery advert
body:
Image source, HandoutsImage caption, Meranda suffered skin irritation after buying a necklace sold as sterling silverByGeorge SandemanJewellery advertised as sterling silver on popular online marketplaces was found to contain toxic chemicals, following a BBC investigation.Some 25 items - bought from Amazon, eBay, Temu, Etsy and OnBuy - were examined by experts for BBC Watchdog on The One Show.Laboratory analysis found eight contained illegal levels of cadmium - a chemical that can cause cancer. Only two items could be classified as sterling silver.Amazon, eBay, Temu and OnBuy said misleading listings were prohibited and that it had removed the jewellery identified by Watchdog. Etsy did not respond.Toxic Jewellery - Watchdog on The One ShowTempted by cheap jewellery advertised as 925 or sterling silver? A Watchdog investigation into if they are genuine finds some contain toxic chemicals.The story about toxic jewellery starts at 01:50
Meranda, 34, bought a necklace advertised on Etsy as handmade sterling silver but says after a few days of wearing it her "neck started getting really irritated"."I remember looking at it as I took it off and thinking the colour on this doesn't look right."Meranda's necklace and the 25 other pieces purchased by Watchdog were analysed by the Sheffield Assay Office.According to preliminary testing, Meranda's necklace was found to contain nickel - another toxic chemical that can cause skin irritation. There are strict legal limits on how much nickel jewellery can contain. Image caption, Watchdog bought five items of jewellery, advertised as 925 or sterling silver, from five online marketplaces to analyseMeranda's necklace was found to have traces of nickel but in one part of the chain the concentration was as high as 11%. Sterling silver jewellery does not typically contain nickel but it is found in some cheaper items.Of the 25 pieces of jewellery bought by Watchdog - which included items like a bracelet for £1.55 and earrings for £1.99 -  eight items contained levels of cadmium over the legal limit of 0.01%.Some had up to 10% cadmium. "[That] is absolutely massive, relative to the limits we're adhering to," says Sophie Langley, who led the analysis.How to spot fake sterling silver Morning Live's consumer expert Rebecca Wilcox shares her tips on how to make sure you're buying the real deal:Cadmium is a carcinogen associated particularly with lung cancer, says Rob Chilcott, a retired professor of toxicology.It poses a risk to humans if it is inhaled or ingested. For example, an earring falling into food that you then eat."If you put something containing cadmium in your mouth, or indeed if you swallow it, that is really bad news," he says.Of the eight items found to have breached cadmium limits: three were purchased from Amazon, three from Temu and one from each of OnBuy and Etsy.Meranda says she had no reason to suspect there was anything wrong with her necklace when she first received it."It was very shiny. It looked legit," she says. "I did not think it wasn't sterling silver."It was hallmarked with the number 925. Genuine sterling silver must contain at least 92.5% silver.However testing revealed part of her necklace contained only 8.9% silver.Selling fake sterling silver is a breach of the Hallmarking Act and carries the risk of fines or imprisonment, says Langley.Image caption, A listing for one of the necklaces tested by Watchdog that was subsequently recalledTemu told the BBC it had arranged testing of similar products to identify potential risks. Amazon and eBay said customers with any concerns should contact them for support. Amazon has since issued recall notices for the products Watchdog identified as being unsafe.OnBuy told us it had offered affected customers refunds and initiated a recall of the product our analysis identified as containing cadmium. Etsy did not respond.Meranda contacted the Etsy seller about the £15 necklace that had irritated her neck. After speaking to Watchdog, she received a full refund.

schema.headline: Jewellery sold as sterling silver on Amazon and Temu found to contain toxic chemicals

title: Thierno Barry's revival: From nightmare debut season to Everton hero
description: Last season Thierno Barry scored eight goals in 41 appearances.This season it's taken him just 12 games to match that tally.On Monday night Barry scor
body: Last season Thierno Barry scored eight goals in 41 appearances.This season it's taken him just 12 games to match that tally.On Monday night Barry scored against Newcastle for the second time in five days as his side earned a deserved win at St James' Park in the Premier League.Only Erling Haaland (13) has scored more goals among Premier League players in all competitions this season than Barry (eight).The 24-year-old is on his best run of form since joining the club from Villarreal last summer and, as Everton's only recognised senior striker following Beto's transfer to Fiorentina, is currently indispensable to the Toffees.By scoring once again Barry highlighted why Everton paid £27m for a striker who grew up watching Wayne Rooney and Romelu Lukaku score for the Toffees.The Frenchman had a rough start to life on Merseyside, having just one shot across his first 16 Everton games, and last month posted a video of himself breaking down during a private training session last season.That moment was contrasted by his celebration on Monday night, which started with a knee slide and ended with dance moves."I was working a lot during the summer and now we can see the result," Barry told  Sky Sports."The season is long but I'm happy to help the team with my goals."I want to enjoy more than last season and I enjoyed my celebration so I am happy."It was a controversial strike though with Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle telling BBC Sport there was "a clear foul on Fabian Schar" in the build-up.

schema.headline: Thierno Barry's revival: From nightmare debut season to Everton hero

title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
description: Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, on Monday told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and
body: Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, on Monday told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and that the company had been "working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network".He said since the French attack in early October, the company had been working to "protect our customers fridges against this vulnerability" but that the units needed physical modifications, not just software updates.Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, and maintenance and troubleshooting can be done remotely."The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France," Moelans added.The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C (122F).It is unclear who is behind the latest apparent attack.In the US, authorities are investigating what caused refrigeration malfunctions at a number of American military bases in August and working together with French officials to examine whether the incidents could be linked.Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident.The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident". No incidents have been reported in the UK.In Flanders, northern Belgium, a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told news website Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost €100,000 (£83,500) worth of produce. The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop.Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said the incident had only affected 15 of its Belgian stores, adding that measures had been taken immediately to ensure all shops remained open.A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, told Reuters news agency five shops had their fridge systems attacked.Sweden's budget furniture retailer Ikea said refrigeration systems of its store in the western Belgian city of Mons were affected, with a spokesman quoted by Reuters as saying "we cannot rule out that additional locations may be affected".In Sweden, several ICA and Coop shops were hit. A spokesperson for ICA confirmed the incident had affected a "small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA's central network"."ICA is currently supporting the affected stores in managing the situation," they said.One of the ICA branches located in Sjöbo, southern Sweden, wrote on social media: "Our refrigerators and freezers have been hacked overnight and they have set the temperature to 50 degrees."The store was closed earlier but has now reopened to customers.Seven out of the 800 Coop stores in Sweden were also affected but the "situation is currently contained and under control", the company told the BBC.In neighbouring Finland, refrigerator malfunctions were detected in some K-stores. The owner of the supermarket chain Kesko was quoted by Finland's Helsingin Sanomat newspaper as saying its security experts were investigating what caused the problem.The attack is also affecting shops in Ireland, the Netherlands and Estonia.In Ireland, it impacted 13 SuperValu supermarkets. A spokesman for the owner of the chain, Musgrave Group, confirmed to The Irish Times that a "cyber incident" affected its refrigeration systems, but added that the impact was limited to a "specific model" of refrigerator.A spokesperson for Danish manufacturer Danfoss told Dutch public radio channel NOS that the freezing and cooling systems of at least 17 companies in the Netherlands were attacked overnight, affecting butcher shops and small neighbourhood stores.A Selver supermarket in Estonia was also affected and there are reports of other affected companies in the country, according to ERR.Additional reporting by Shiona McCallumHave you been affected by the issues raised in this story? title: Troy Deeney's Team of the Week: Rice, Konsa, Van Hecke, McBurnie
description: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give
body: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.Bart Verbruggen (Brighton): He was unreal. Lots of saves which kept Brighton in it, even the last-ditch save where it hit him in the face.Just an impenetrable wall. Brighton should really have lost by two or three goals, but Verbruggen was the reason they didn't.Archie Gray (Tottenham): I'm going with a fully north London back four. Gray scored and defended really well. He was under a lot of pressure when Tottenham were in bad form and got a lot of stick, but now Spurs are starting to pick up I'm going to give him a bit of credit. Ezri Konsa (Arsenal): He was a beast. Head it, kick it, throw your body in front of the ball. He defended and fought for the team, getting the job done.Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham): Van Hecke got a goal and he's really growing into his role at Spurs. I still think he was a little bit overpriced, but all in all he's had a solid start, coming up with a few goals. Micky van de Ven next to him gives him confidence that he can go and be really aggressive, because Van der Ven will cover him with his pace.Jurrien Timber (Arsenal): Timber got away with a shirt pull on Alexander Isak and I'm really surprised the ref and video assistant referee (VAR) didn't look at it. But again I thought he recovered and defended really well at full-back.Romeo Lavia (Chelsea): I thought Lavia was excellent for Chelsea. People will turn to Manchester United having 10 men, but the 60 minutes before that Chelsea were all over the place. Lavia was the only constant breaking up play, keeping the ball moving. Plus he had an assist. Declan Rice (Arsenal): A proper captain's performance, he gets the job done all over the pitch. He got a little assist for himself, too. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto (Coventry): Sakamoto goes unnoticed by a lot of people, but I think he works really hard for the team and he is very humble in his approach. On Saturday he also delivered in a massive game for his team.Johan Manzambi (Aston Villa): Another assist for him. He's a 21-year-old who is just flying. His confidence is through the roof and he is taking over this Villa team. Really good player, only going to get better. He was taken off thinking about the Champions League game against Barcelona, but up until that point Fulham couldn't really stop him.Ollie McBurnie (Hull): Grafter, scrappy, endeavour, goals, assists... He had it all in his game. He epitomises what Hull are: a player that's always overlooked, a team that's always overlooked, but they've got some spirit, some fight.Taiwo Awoniyi (Coventry): Unbelievable solo goal. It's really good to see the big fella back playing and being in a situation where he can impose himself. If Coventry are to stay up, he's going to be why.Frank Lampard (Coventry): He has been really good. Coventry have taken care of business against Sunderland, it's a massive six-pointer those games and his team came out front-footed, aggressive and also did a job on a very good Sunderland team.Also a massive nod to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta for getting the job done at Liverpool.Do you agree with Troy's selections? Who would be in your Team of the Week? Have your say using the comments form below:

title: Man Utd's Michael Carrick says it's 'crazy' but he's looking forward to Roma game
description: Michael Carrick accepts it might sound "crazy" but the beleaguered Manchester United boss says he is looking forward to the Champions League showdown
body: Michael Carrick accepts it might sound "crazy" but the beleaguered Manchester United boss says he is looking forward to the Champions League showdown with Roma at Old Trafford.United go into Tuesday's game without a win in nine matches in all competitions.It is their worst run since 1988-89. They have not gone 10 without a win in a single campaign since 1977-78 and there is a growing feeling Carrick will lose his job during the forthcoming international break.Roma's only defeat so far this season was at home to Real Madrid in the Champions League last month, when they led 3-1 with seven minutes left.United are 17th in the Premier League and after defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como have slumped to 21st in the Champions League table after three games, with only the top 24 making it through.It is a bleak backdrop, but rather than fret over what lies ahead, Carrick is viewing it as a chance to change the narrative of the season."You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but genuinely, I really can't wait for the game," said Carrick. "I'm really looking forward to it."Listen, I can't look into the future, you never know what's going to happen. That doesn't change the way I feel. Whatever happens is going to happen in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow."Carrick watched over a lively open session of pre-match training at Carrington.Striker Bryan Mbeumo and midfielder Carlos Baleba were particularly vocal, with Argentina defender Lisandro Martinez also fully engaged despite his red card at Chelsea, which triggered such a negative reaction.While there have been calls for Martinez to be dropped for the Roma game, Carrick was more philosophical."Things happen in football," he said."Sometimes you do things; you make a decision, you make mistakes. Sometimes it goes well for you."He also dismissed concerns both about Martinez's commitment, and that of his entire squad."Perceptions are a funny thing," he said."They can make things look all sorts of different ways. The dressing room is a good place."I've said it before, I don't question the commitment of the players, to the club and to me and to each other. We need to play better. We can make better decisions. But commitment's not a thing at all."England midfielder Kobbie Mainoo sat alongside Carrick at the media conference and also stressed the strength of the group.Mainoo returned from a four-match absence with a muscular issue as a second-half substitute at Chelsea.At 21, Mainoo is one of the youngest players in Carrick's squad. However, given he joined the club as a seven-year-old, he is also the longest serving and has a unique insight into the responsibilities that come with life in the Old Trafford spotlight."I've been at this club for a long time and know there's always going to be ups and downs," he said. "It's never going to be plain sailing and smooth to the top. You expect bumps."Of course it's been a tough season. We've not had the results we've wanted, but I feel like we're one win away from changing that."United were last relegated in 1973-74. They have not been in the relegation zone after nine games or more since November 1986, when they collected a single point in Sir Alex Ferguson's first two games in charge following Ron Atkinson's dismissal.Their lowest position after at least nine games of a season since then was 17th in 1989-90. They were 16th under Ruben Amorim after 37 games of the 2024-25 season.Mainoo says the present position is unacceptable for a club of United's size."United's a huge club," he said. "I think a lot of people know the values this club holds and have been passed down through the people who've worked here and played here."I feel like I take some responsibility in spreading the word of what Manchester United is, coming up through the academy, and I plan to send that message for as long as I can."

schema.headline: Man Utd's Michael Carrick says it's 'crazy' but he's looking forward to Roma game

title: Prosecutors hint at plans to retry Lindsay Clancy on murder charges
description: Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of attempted suicideMassachusetts prosecutors have given their clearest indication yet
body: Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of attempted suicideMassachusetts prosecutors have given their clearest indication yet that they plan to retry Lindsay Clancy for the murder of her three children in 2023.At a hearing on Monday, Judge William Sullivan scheduled a 16 November hearing where he plans to rule on a handful of motions that could determine how a retrial would proceed, including a request to dismiss the first-degree murder charges.Clancy faced a weekslong trial on those charges over the summer. It fell apart in early September after a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict. If there is a retrial, Judge Sullivan said, it could happen as soon as March 2027.The prosecution did not say on Monday whether Clancy would face the same charges or amended charges in the event of a retrial. When the parties meet again later this month, they will hear the judge's rulings on the motions argued in court on Monday, and potentially will discuss dates for a retrial, Judge Sullivan said.Kevin Reddington, Clancy's attorney, pushed the judge for a spring trial."I am not going to have this woman sit incarcerated for the next year or two or three," he said. "I want a date and I want it this spring."But prosecutor Jennifer Sprague said she wants to hear Judge Sullivan's rulings on   Monday's arguments before the prosecution commits to a new date or specifics for a potential retrial.When the judge asked for more details on how prosecutors planned to proceed with a potential retrial, Sprague responded: "This would be a retrial - as to what that looks like will depend". But that appeared to frustrate Reddington. "Why do we not know if the next trial is going to be murder in the first degree or a lesser charge, why do they need to wait for the motions? I need to know logistically."Clancy was charged with three counts of first-degree-murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.Prosecutors could decide to bring lesser charges against Clancy in a retrial. For example, second-degree-murder charges, apply to unlawful killings committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without prior planning.Despite Sprague's statement in court, District Attorney Timothy Cruz has not yet   confirmed that Clancy will face a retrial and has not announced future plans for the case. Much of Monday's conversations in court focused on the one holdout juror, also known as Juror Doe, and the defence's investigation into him. Juror Doe disagreed with the other jurors, who appeared to want to find Clancy not guilty by way of insanity. The lack of agreement led to a hung jury and mistrial.In some of the most fiery moments of the three-hour hearing on Monday, Reddington requested a plethora of evidence including the holdout juror's phone and phone records. Heather O'Connor, the attorney who represents Juror Doe, said she was in court because Clancy's defence team has "combined several allegations" to try to argue that a mistrial should not have been declared, she said.That is among the motions Sullivan said he will rule on in a few weeks.Clancy does not deny killing her children, but her defence team argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. Prosecutors claim the killings were intentional.

schema.headline: Prosecutors hint at plans to retry Lindsay Clancy on murder charges

title: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators
description: It confirmed that, after the jet took off from Austin, the crew transmitted to air traffic control that they were encountering ice and moderate turbul
body: It confirmed that, after the jet took off from Austin, the crew transmitted to air traffic control that they were encountering ice and moderate turbulence."We are picking up precipitation, requesting to climb to 37,000 feet if able," the crew said.NTSB member Tom Chapman said that less than 30 seconds later, the plane began to descend and the crew issued a mayday call.The transmission then became "unintelligible", he said, adding that: "Sadly, all aboard were lost."The NTSB said that ice and turbulence were factors in the crash but that determining its probable cause will be a "lengthy investigatory process".Thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time. Officials are also trying to find out whether a cockpit voice recorder was on board at the time of the crash and if it can be recovered.As part of the investigation, the NTSB is working with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), representatives from Learjet as well as meteorologists and air traffic control experts.Recovering the wreckage from the crater on the roadway will be a "daunting challenge", said Timothy Monville, an air safety investigator with the safety board.Flight analysis indicates the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing.In air traffic control audio, a crew member can be heard declaring an emergency, shouting "we are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000ft per minute", before saying, "we are going to crash into the ground".About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last remark from the cockpit appears to be "we're out of time".The seven people killed who were travelling as passengers were identified in a joint statement from their families as tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp, and their two children - Emma and Charlie - as well as Rachael Reed, Charmi Fehr and Anita Maria Cetina.The pilot was named in media reports as Jeffery Gregory, while Nathalia Filgueiras, who earned her pilot's licence when she was 17, was reported to be the copilot. As well as those killed, one man on the ground sustained a leg injury when the plane nosedived onto the street.

schema.headline: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators

title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's request to stop California counting disputed votes
description: Image source, Getty ImagesBySareen HabeshianReporting fromLos AngelesThe US Supreme Court has rejected a last-minute request by the Trump administrati
body: Image source, Getty ImagesBySareen HabeshianReporting fromLos AngelesThe US Supreme Court has rejected a last-minute request by the Trump administration asking it to intervene in California's midterm election vote count. The justice department wanted 20,000 ballots to be set aside that it alleged may have been issued to non-US citizens in the state. Two lower courts had already rejected the request. State election officials had questioned the federal government's claims - saying the process used to identify alleged non-citizens was inaccurate. The Monday ruling comes on the eve of the midterms, which will determine which political party controls the US Congress for the last two years of President Donald Trump's second term. The Supreme Court announced its decision in a one-line order, saying it was denying the justice department's request for an injunction. "The application for injunction pending appeal presented to Justice Kagan and by her referred to the Court is denied," it reads.Its means rulings made in lower courts will stand and essentially ends the Trump administration's bid to disqualify the ballots. California is the most populous state in America with some 23 million people on its voting register. As of Sunday night, more than six million mail-in ballots had already been received, according to the California secretary of state's office.The justice department sent letters to the California secretary of state and Los Angeles County Registrar last month, demanding they set aside the ballots of 20,000 registered voters whom the Trump administration "believe" are "likely" non-citizens, according to court documents.About a week later, armed officials from the Department of Homeland Security delivered letters to county officials and employees across California threatening criminal charges if they didn't sequester those ballots.In a 22-page brief reviewed by the BBC, the justice department maintained that ballots cast by non-citizens could "debase or dilute valid votes".On Friday, a federal appeals court declined the government's request to segregate the ballots.California election officials have questioned the accuracy of the government's claims, and have said the list of names the government has provided is riddled with inaccuracies.They have expressed concern that eligible voters could be disenfranchised and said segregating ballots whilst voting is underway is unfeasible. Figure caption, What are Americans voting for this election?The attempts are a part of a years-long campaign by Trump and his administration to fight alleged voter fraud that they believe is widespread, despite research showing that it is extremely rare.President Trump has repeatedly claimed that Democrats steal elections by allowing immigrants to vote illegally, and he blames much of it on the so-called "mail-in" or postal voting that is permitted in many Democratic states.Last week in a scathing ruling, district judge David Carter said the government's move in California was indicative of an "ongoing pattern of attempted election interference" on the part of the Trump administration.The judge added that "never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the executive branch". With additional reporting by the BBC's David Willis

schema.headline: Supreme Court rejects Trump's request to stop California counting disputed votes

title: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
description: The UK and EU have agreed a draft deal on removing post-Brexit checks from food and agriculture exports, ahead of the UK-EU summit later this month.Th
body: The UK and EU have agreed a draft deal on removing post-Brexit checks from food and agriculture exports, ahead of the UK-EU summit later this month.The BBC understands the 200-page draft text for this so called "SPS" [sanitary and phytosanitary] agreement has been circulated to EU nations in Brussels for consideration at a meeting on Wednesday.Similar texts for deals on emissions trading and a youth travel and work scheme have also been circulated alongside a 15-page draft joint statement for UK and EU top leaders.The food deal is the most significant part of the so-called Brexit reset agreed so far, removing checks and red tape that hit exporters after the UK exited the EU's single market.The deal should remove the need for £200 Export Health Certificates, £25 Phytosanitary certificates, inspector fees, organic certificates, some port fees, sampling fees and other checks for exports and imports to and from the EU. The government claims the UK economy will eventually see £5.1bn worth of annual benefits.UK exports to the EU of fresh sausages, burgers, shellfish from domestic waters and seed potatoes will also be able to resume.The agreement will also allow for passports for UK pets taken into the EU.Under the agreement the UK will commit to observing and adapting to existing EU regulations on plant, animal and food trade standards. This process is called "dynamic alignment".While UK rules remain mostly aligned with EU ones, there are some areas where England has diverged from the EU rule book, for example on "precision breeding" of plants, previously known as gene editing. In recent weeks, agreement has been struck on transition arrangements while the EU's new regulations come in to force.The government has already announced a European Partnerships Bill which will provide a legal mechanism for the application of new EU rules and regulations. This will also allow for the necessary alignments for the linking of the UK emissions trading scheme with the EU's, and save the need for UK exporters to pay the EU's new carbon border tax.The draft agreements will be discussed at a meeting of EU ambassadors called Coreper on Wednesday, with some key details on the planned numbers in a Youth Experience Scheme to be finalised at a political level in the coming days. A discount on full foreign student fees for EU students is likely to be pushed to next year alongside a plan to reconnect electricity markets.The BBC understands that the draft agreements will also include some references to UK involvement in defence cooperation schemes, access to law enforcement databases and some reassurances over the EU's "Made in Europe" plans.While the food trade plans have been backed by supermarkets and farmers representatives, some pro-Brexit campaigners have criticised the reapplication of EU rules. The post-Brexit trade deal signed by Boris Johnson's government prioritised regulatory freedoms for the UK over avoiding new regulatory red tape, checks and delays.The British Chamber of Commerce released a new analysis of its members' views on Monday suggesting options for a closer relationship. The business lobby group says the current trade relationship is "failing to deliver", leaving firms "struggling with a thicket of Brexit red tape" nearly six years after the UK's exit from the bloc.It also pointed to economic analysis of more fundamental changes to the UK-EU relationship, suggesting the largest long-term economic boosts from rejoining the single market or the EU itself. The BCC called on government to analyse and publish options, as it consults its members.The BCC is calling for an exploration of what a new relationship could look like, and offers nine options, including a customs union, a "Swiss-style" Single Market relationship, and a "Canada model" associate membership."The evidence from businesses suggests that the prime minister is right to have initiated a conversation on our future relationship with Europe, and he deserves real credit for having done so."Government needs to examine all of the options, remain clear-headed about the trade-offs each involves, and involve business in the decision-making process from the start," Shevaun Havilland, director general of the BCC, said.More than half (56%) of exporting businesses in a BCC survey said they wanted EU customs paperwork and delays removed so they can grow. That rose to 58% of manufacturers.The prime minister has said he wants to use this month's summit to launch a conversation on a longer term path for the UK's relationship with the EU, including "going all the way", meaning rejoining the bloc.

schema.headline: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports

title: 'Mogging' is Collins' word of the year... but do you know what it means?
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Mogging is about playfully upstaging someone or somethingByPaul GlynnCulture reporter"Mogging", a word used p
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Mogging is about playfully upstaging someone or somethingByPaul GlynnCulture reporter"Mogging", a word used playfully to mean outshining, outperforming or upstaging someone or something, has been named as word of the year by the Collins English Dictionary.A fast-growing slang word among members of Generations Z and Alpha - both online and in everyday conversation - mogging went mainstream in 2026 with a 210% increase in its usage.Collins' managing director Alex Beecroft said its lexicographers look at "how often words are used" and also "analyse patterns of usage" that reveal the latest linguistic trends.The selection of mogging as word of the year, he said, "shows how each generation leaves its mark on language".Image source, CollinsImage caption, Mogging the Mona Lisa, whatever next?He added: "It's a great example of how Gen Z and Gen Alpha have adopted a word and turned it into humorous slang, making the language their own and 'mogging' the rest of us!"Mogging - not to be confused with mugging or mugging someone off - refers to outshining or dominating someone, most often in looks.You may even have mogged someone or been mogged yourself over the past 12 months.The word is often traced back to the acronym AMOG, standing for Alpha Male of the Group, and has been variously associated with bodybuilding forums in the mid-2010s as well as the manosphere and incels.But it now has a much more mainstream usage, as a playful put-down or a compliment, depending on the context.It can be seen and heard in looksmaxxing communities -online groups where people swap advice on how to maximise their physical attractiveness.Collins - one of the UK's major dictionary publishers - draws from a range of sources, including social media, to reflect how the English language is evolving in the UK each year.Its word of the year for 2025 was "vibe coding" - the art of making an app or website by describing it to artificial intelligence (AI) rather than by writing programming code manually.Other definitions that made the dictionary's 10-strong shortlist included ghost job, something frustrated jobseekers will be familiar with - when an employer posts a position with no intention of appointing someone.Hydration break was of course made famous by this year's World Cup. while p(doom) is the estimation of probability of an AI-aided collapse of civilisation. Manchesterism, a term associated with Prime Minister Andy Burnham, is about the devolution of power to the regions, combining economic growth withh social progress.

title: Legal challenge to Australia's social media ban to start in High Court
description: Two days of hearings on a challenge to Australia's landmark social media ban for children will begin at the country's highest court on Tuesday.In a ma
body: Two days of hearings on a challenge to Australia's landmark social media ban for children will begin at the country's highest court on Tuesday.In a major test of the world-leading policy, a digital rights group will argue that the ban for under-16s robs children of their right to free communication. A separate challenge launched by platform Reddit will be jointly heard.Introduced last December, the ban is a key part of sweeping changes the Australian government has spearheaded in recent years on online safety.Supporters say the ban protects children from harmful content but critics say it is too blunt an instrument and efforts should focus on improving online safety.The constitutional challenge in Australia's High Court was filed by the Digital Freedom Project a few weeks before the ban started on 10 December last year. The group is lead by New South Wales parliamentarian John Ruddick.Two teens who originally spearheaded the case, Noah Jones and Macy Neyland, have since withdrawn as plaintiffs though Jones is still expected to attend Tuesday's hearing.Speaking about the legal challenge last November, Jones told the BBC that there were bad things online but a blanket ban for under-16s was not the right answer. "We shouldn't be using the resources and money of these social media platforms to try to avoid fines from our government," he said."They should be using this money and resources to try to get rid of the predators and harmful content out there."Reddit also launched a High Court challenge to the ban, arguing the policy has serious implications for privacy and political rights.The company said it shared Australia's goal of protecting young people online "but there are better and more effective ways" than a ban."As we challenge this law in court, we'll continue to comply with it and advocate for more effective youth safety measures," said Reddit's chief communications officer Adam Collins.Communications Minister Anika Wells last year said the government would not be "intimidated by legal threats." "We will not be intimidated by big tech. On behalf of Australian parents, we will stand firm," she said last November. Under the ban, ten platforms - Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Snapchat, X, Kick, Threads and Twitch - must take "reasonable steps" to ensure no one under 16 years old can access its site.Platforms risk fines of up to A$99m (US$70m, £52m) for serious or repeated breaches, but since the ban started, no company has been fined.

title: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers
description: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has scrapped plans to make foreign care workers already in the UK wait 15 years to qualify for permanent settlement.Mah
body: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has scrapped plans to make foreign care workers already in the UK wait 15 years to qualify for permanent settlement.Mahmood had proposed doubling the wait for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) from five years to 10 for most migrants, with some facing a 15-year wait.But following a backlash from several Labour MPs, Mahmood revised the policy and care workers who earn at least £25,000 a year and arrived in the UK before May 2025 would continue to qualify after five years.The Conservatives said Mahmood's "U-turn" would cost taxpayers billions of pounds.ILR, also known as settlement, gives a person the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like and apply for benefits if they are eligible. They can also use it to apply for British citizenship.Last November, Mahmood announced plans to delay settlements in response to concerns over the number of people approaching eligibility, in the wake of record post-Brexit net migration figures under the previous Conservative government, nicknamed the "Boriswave".Asked by the BBC whether she had u-turned on her earlier promises, she replied "I don't accept that", adding that some 500,000 people in the UK "will not now settle at five years"."They will have to wait longer before they can achieve settlement in this country, and I've come to a fair resolution for care workers," she said.The home secretary refused to say what the cost will be of scrapping her plans.When she put forward the original plans in March, the Home Office used data from the committee which advises ministers on migration to forecast that the existing rules would cost £4.2bn. This was the estimated lifetime cost of the 117,000 foreign care workers expected to settle in the UK from 2026-2030. It estimated this would rise to £9.5bn once their adult dependants were factored in.Mahmood told the BBC updated plans would save "billions", partly because workers in other sectors will still have to wait longer, but said an impact assessment detailing the cost would be released in a future announcement.She also declined to outline whether Prime Minister Andy Burnham had told her to change tack on her proposals, which she had put forward under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer, saying a consultation had resulted in a fair settlement.The Conservatives said her "U-turn" will cost the state billions of pounds.The Home Office has said its figures show net migration - the difference between those entering and leaving the country - added 2.6m people to the UK population between 2021 and 2024.The department estimates that between 2026 and 2030 between 1.3m and 2.2m people will settle in the UK, adding its central estimate has increased to 1.9m.The home secretary faced criticism for proposing to apply the changes to migrant workers already in the UK, with Housing Secretary Angela Rayner previously saying this would "change the goalposts".Several Labour MPs also described the retrospective approach as "un-British" and  warned it could worsen the UK's skills shortage, particularly in the care sector.Making a statement to the House of Commons, Mahmood said settlement "should not be automatic, it should be earned".The changes will move those earning less than £50,000 a year onto a 10-year path to settlement status, unless they are exempt.Mahmood also told MPs the government would provide a five-year path to settlement for care workers who "answered our call when we needed them" following the Covid-19 pandemic.Mahmood said: "Those who earn £25,000 a year working in the social care sector, which was the condition of their visa, will therefore be able to settle on their existing five-year path."She added those care workers who did not meet the conditions of their visa could apply for another five-year visa and seek settlement after that.MPs were also told: higher earners on salaries of more than £50,000 and those who have contributed in healthcare and education, such as doctors and teachers, will be able to qualify for settlement after five yearsthe highest rate taxpayers earning more than £125,000 will be able to apply after three yearsrefugees who arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they do not.Mahmood said: "Our changes ensure those who are net contributors are encouraged to come to this country and stay here."She added: "As a result, the Department for Work and Pensions estimates that our reforms will reduce the benefits bill by billions of pounds."The original version of the plans announced by Mahmood last year would have delayed 799,000 people from gaining permanent residency. Under the updated plans announced on Monday, that number would drop to 517,000.One of those affected was Ashfak Juned, a Bangladeshi chef working in Birmingham, who told the BBC he was  "crying" when he heard his wait for settled status would now last until 2033.The home secretary also confirmed a number of groups would see their settlement path remain as it is today - including Hong Kong British nationals overseas, armed forces members, people with a British connection and those on legacy routes including the Windrush scheme.The Refugee Council's Imran Hussain said the plans for those who had travelled to the UK illegally or by small boat and do not work or study to wait 30 years for ILR were "unfair and unworkable"."The fairest reforms would be making fast and good quality asylum decisions, with those refugees granted protection being helped to rebuild their lives and to contribute, and those with no right to remain helped to leave with dignity," he said.For the Conservatives, shadow home secretary Chris Philp said opposition from Mahmood's fellow ministers and the "Labour open borders left" had resulted in the changes from Mahmood's original proposals, adding that she was "no longer running the government's immigration policy".He highlighted figures from March in which Home Office calculations suggested the estimated lifetime cost of £9.5bn to taxpayers.Philp said this was the "cost of today's U-turn".But Father of the House Sir Edward Leigh, the longest-serving male MP in the Commons, criticised his Conservative colleague for overseeing the so-called Boriswave after Brexit, where net migration peaked at nearly one million in 2023."Some of us don't have amnesia," he said.Liberal Democrat home affairs spokesman Max Wilkinson said the government's reforms were "unravelling".He added: "Viewing immigration simply as a matter of raw numbers and images of small boat arrivals is degrading this nation's ability to have the informed national discussion that we need."Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said Mahmood had "shown her true colours"."She talked a big game on immigration but has u-turned at the first sign of trouble from her left wing Labour colleagues," he said.Pointing to Home Office estimates that more than 200,000 immigrants arriving on Health and Care visas would be eligible for British citizenship before the next election, he claimed this would cost the taxpayer £50bn over their lifetimes.He vowed to review citizenship of all those arriving on care visas from today and extend the qualifying period for citizenship to a minimum of 10 years.Green Party MP Siân Berry said Mahmood had provided a "new obstacle course of hoops and barriers" for migrants living in the UK.On Monday, the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank said that skilled workers and their dependants due to settle in the UK under current rules are expected to make a net lifetime contribution of around £115bn through the taxes they pay.

schema.headline: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers

title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at humanitarian aid centre in Ukraine, Kyiv says
description: Meanwhile, Semikin described the Russian attack as a "terrible tragedy" for the village, confirming that "people are still under the rubble". He said
body: Meanwhile, Semikin described the Russian attack as a "terrible tragedy" for the village, confirming that "people are still under the rubble". He said rescue teams were working at the scene, but they had been forced to halt their operation a number of times because of Russian drone attacks in the area.A day of mourning has been declared for Tuesday across the entire Zaporizhzhia region.Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.Teams from Ukraine, Russia and the US are due to resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates, next week, US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff said on X.Since the talks were suspended in February, Moscow has stepped up attacks as Kyiv virtually ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles.No major breakthrough is expected at the talks. Witkoff said the discussions would focus on "post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace".Witkoff said US negotiators would also meet European and Nato officials this week in Brussels.

title: F1: George Russell on 'tough' season after Kimi Antonelli wins title
description: George Russell says his struggles in 2026 while Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli marched to the drivers' title have been "tough to deal with" and had
body: George Russell says his struggles in 2026 while Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli marched to the drivers' title have been "tough to deal with" and had left him "often confused".Russell started the season as favourite and won the first race, but soon started to struggle as Antonelli built up unstoppable momentum.In a post on Instagram, the Briton congratulated Antonelli "on what has been an absolutely incredible season" and said the Italian "truly deserved the championship".Russell added: "Now feels like a pretty suitable moment to speak from the heart."This season started off exactly how I had hoped but it very quickly unravelled with tough luck and poor performances."It's been the first proper season of my career where I've had more bad days than good."Has it been tough to deal with? Yes, very."Has it been tough to pick myself up week in, week out? Yes, very."Confusion at times? Often."All I know is that I've given it my all and 2026 was not meant to be my year."Russell has won three races to Antonelli's nine, and finishing sixth in the Mexico City Grand Prix on Sunday while Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton finished first and second ahead of Antonelli meant he slipped to fourth in the championship as the Dutchman moved up to second ahead of Hamilton.The Mexico race was the latest example of Russell, who started second behind Hamilton, suffering tough luck.A glitch in energy deployment off the start line left him down on power, and he was swamped by the field.A misjudgment then led to his hitting Red Bull's Isack Hadjar at Turn Six and tipping him into a spin. For that, Russell was given a 10-second penalty.Russell thanked his team for "producing the best car and power-unit this season" and said it had been "inspiring to see everyone coming together over four tough years to bring Mercedes back to the top".He had gone into the race knowing it was highly likely Antonelli would clinch the title, but afterwards emotions overwhelmed him and he was close to tears while being weighed.Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff saw the Briton at that point and allowed him to miss his post-race media duties.Wolff said: "I saw George after the race on the FIA scales. And obviously, he's distraught about the situation. It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi."I have known George for such a long time. And I know, for a sportsperson, he's going through a hard time, but he was also responsible in getting the young man into this team."And so I'm very much with him at the moment. I've been in situations where he's very, very difficult to cope. So him not doing the media work or leaving the track is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me. So that's absolutely on. Yeah, we said he can go."Russell added on instagram: "Now all I can promise is that for the rest of this season and into the next one I will be giving my absolute all to rediscover the performance I have been capable of for the majority of my career and fingers crossed a little bit of luck returns."Antonelli said of Russell after the race: "Definitely I think he has had also bad luck at some point in the season. He said a little bit more than me, being honest."But still he will definitely come back. He's super-quick. He has shown this season that when he's on it, he's very hard to beat. So it's just about, on my side, keep focusing on myself, keep trying to raise the bar, keep improving, keep developing because it's not going to be only a matter of George at the end of the season."Also for next season Red Bull, especially with Max, Ferrari and McLaren eventually, we're all going to be up there and it's going to be a tight fight so it's going to be important to be on top of the game, not only against my team-mate but against also all the others."

schema.headline: F1: George Russell on 'tough' season after Kimi Antonelli wins title
